name: Hebrew
signature: Right-to-left, but blocky and separate — squarish letters sitting apart, not joined into a cursive.
combination: Written right-to-left. Letters are consonants; vowels are usually left UNwritten (modern Hebrew), or shown as small dots/lines called niqqud above, below, or inside a letter. Letters do NOT join cursively (unlike Arabic), but five letters take a special FINAL form when they end a word: כ→ך, מ→ם, נ→ן, פ→ף, צ→ץ. A dagesh (dot inside) hardens some letters (ב v→b, כ kh→k, פ f→p).
notes: The 22-letter Hebrew alphabet with final forms and the main niqqud. Marked complete:false only because the niqqud set here is the common core, not exhaustive; the letters themselves are complete. Descended from the same Phoenician source as Greek and Latin, so the letter ORDER and names are cousins: alef↔alpha↔A, bet↔beta↔B, gimel↔gamma↔C/G.

letters.notes: Carries whatever vowel sits with it; no consonant sound of its own.

components: a base with a little foot sticking right
letters.notes: With a dagesh (בּ) = b; without = v. The base foot distinguishes it from כ.

components: a small left foot at the base

letters.notes: Vs ר: ד has a sharp top-right corner/heel; ר is rounded.

components: a separate short left leg (with a GAP at the top-left)
letters.notes: Vs ח: ה has a gap at top-left; ח is closed.

components: a single vertical stroke with a small head
letters.notes: Also carries the long vowels o/u. Vs ז and final ן.

components: two legs joined by a top bar (a closed gate)
letters.notes: Closed at the top, unlike ה.

components: an inward hook at the top-left
a small stroke floating at the TOP of the line
letters.notes: The smallest letter. Also carries the vowel i.

components: a top bar curving down into a rounded base (like a backwards C)
letters.notes: Final form ך drops straight below the line. Dagesh (כּ) = k; without = kh. Vs ב (no base foot).

components: a tall stroke rising ABOVE the line
letters.notes: The only letter that rises above the top line.

components: a right part with a small gap at the bottom-left
letters.notes: Final ם is a closed square box.

components: a foot turning right at the base
letters.notes: Final ן is a straight stroke dropping below the line.
Vs final ם: ס is rounder/closed on all sides.

components: meeting in a V at the base
letters.notes: Like alef, mostly a vowel carrier in modern Hebrew.

components: a top bar curling into an inward spiral (a tucked-in mouth)
letters.notes: Dagesh (פּ) = p; without = f. Final ף drops below the line.

components: an arm reaching up to the right
letters.notes: Final ץ extends below the line.

components: a left leg that DROPS below the line
letters.notes: One of the few non-final letters with a descender.
Vs ד: ר is rounded at the top-right; ד has a sharp heel.

components: three upward branches from a common base (like a W/crown)
letters.notes: A dot upper-RIGHT (שׁ) = sh; upper-LEFT (שׂ) = s.

components: a left leg with a small foot
letters.notes: The last letter (taw). Wider, with two legs.

marks.attachesAs: patach — a short horizontal line BELOW the letter
kamatz — a small T-shape BELOW the letter
segol — three dots in a triangle BELOW the letter
tsere — two dots side by side BELOW the letter
chirik — a single dot BELOW the letter
cholam — a dot at the upper-LEFT of the letter
qubuts — three diagonal dots BELOW the letter
shva — two vertical dots BELOW, a very short or absent vowel
dagesh — a dot INSIDE the letter (בּ=b, כּ=k, פּ=p)
